segments.he: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת, אֲבָל חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי בָתִּים אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה נָמֵי, אִם רָצוּ לְעָרֵב — מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד. מַאי טַעְמָא? בֵּיתָא כְּמַאן דִּמְלֵי דָּמֵי.
segments.en: It was taught in the mishna: If a window is «less than four by four» handbreadths, or if it is above ten handbreadths from the ground, the residents of the two courtyards may not establish one joint eiruv but must instead establish two independent ones. «Rav Naḥman said: They taught» this halakha of a window within ten handbreadths of the ground «only» with regard to «a window between two courtyards. But» with regard to «a window between two houses, even» if it is «above ten» handbreadths «as well, if they wish to establish an eiruv, they establish one eiruv. What is the reason» for this halakha? It is that «a house is considered as though it» were «filled,» and therefore there is no difference between below and above ten handbreadths with regard to a window in a house.
